original_question: Determine whether the conjectured nonlinear instability of Anti-de Sitter spacetime, in which weak turbulence transfers energy to high frequencies and can trigger black hole formation, changes qualitatively in models more general than spherically symmetric scalar-field collapse.
target_in_paper: Problem P8 in §4.1, Instability of Anti-de Sitter spacetime.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official target very closely: it identifies the conjectured nonlinear instability of Anti-de Sitter spacetime, the weakly turbulent transfer of energy to high frequencies, the possible formation of black holes, and the central comparison with models beyond the original spherically symmetric scalar-field-collapse setting.
missing_details: The benchmark model in the nearby discussion is not generic scalar collapse, but spherically symmetric perturbations of a self-gravitating minimally coupled massless scalar field governed by the Einstein-scalar field equations.
The paper places the question in asymptotically Anti-de Sitter spacetimes, not in arbitrary negatively curved backgrounds.
The paper stresses that the stability question depends on the choice of boundary conditions at infinity; any fully stand-alone formulation should acknowledge that this is part of the problem.
The motivating conjecture concerns black-hole formation from a large class of arbitrarily small perturbations in the benchmark model; your draft omits the small-data aspect.
The nearby context sharpens the intended extension to non-spherical perturbations and arbitrary spacetime dimension.

The discussion also ties the weakly turbulent mechanism to secular growth and resonant four-wave interactions, and notes the related open issues of whether a fully resonant/nondispersive linear spectrum is essential and how generic the instability is.
Ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, and phrases such as 'for all sufficiently large m' are not applicable here, because this is a geometric/PDE problem rather than an algebraic one.
refined_question: For asymptotically Anti-de Sitter spacetimes, after fixing boundary conditions at infinity, determine whether the conjectured nonlinear instability of AdS—supported in the spherically symmetric Einstein equations coupled to a self-gravitating minimally coupled massless scalar field, where arbitrarily small perturbations can produce a weakly turbulent cascade toward high frequencies and form arbitrarily small black holes—behaves qualitatively differently in models more general than spherically symmetric scalar-field collapse, especially for non-spherical perturbations and in arbitrary spacetime dimension.
justification: The draft is targeting the paper's officially stated open problem P8 almost verbatim. Section 4.1 first explains the original spherically symmetric Einstein-massless-scalar setting, the weakly turbulent high-frequency cascade, and the possibility of arbitrarily small black-hole formation, then emphasizes that the main extension of interest is beyond spherical symmetry, especially toward non-spherical perturbations in arbitrary dimension. The same nearby discussion also adds a paper-critical hidden assumption that the AdS stability question depends on boundary conditions at infinity. The refined version therefore keeps P8's wording and scope, while making explicit the benchmark model, the small-perturbation regime, the role of boundary conditions, and the intended generalization.
